The refactor is safe to make aggressively — but there is no safety net, so behaviour-preserving arithmetic (which px value maps to which utility) has to be exact rather than eyeballed. - **`tailwind.config.ts` sits right there.** The design system isn't hypothetical — `brand` / `surface` / `ink` are declared. That upgrades `design_token_escape` from "you have no tokens" to "you have tokens and this file routed around them," which is the version that actually misleads an agent extending the file. One thing the config explains: it sets `theme.colors`, not `theme.extend.colors`. That's a hard override — it deletes Tailwind's entire default palette, so there is no `white`, `black`, or `gray-500`. That's plausibly *why* the author reached for `#333333` and `#666666`: the token scale is real but too thin to express the component. So this isn't a mechanical find-and-replace; it needs token *decisions*. --- ## 1. `design_token_escape` → name the values, extend the scale `fingerprint=design_token_escape::src/Card.tsx::` · 9 raw values across 4 kinds Card uses seven distinct colours against a three-colour palette. Four need new tokens: ```ts // tailwind.config.ts export default { theme: { colors: { brand: "#0050ff", surface: "#f7f7fa", ink: "#111111", // promoted out of src/Card.tsx "surface-accent": "#ff00aa", // was: background "ink-strong": "#0a0a0a", // was: color "ink-muted": "#333333", // was: body text "ink-subtle": "#666666", // was: sidebar text border: "#cccccc", focus: "#1a73e8", // was: outlineColor }, boxShadow: { card: "0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0)", }, }, }; ``` I kept the shadow fully opaque to stay behaviour-preserving, but flag it: `rgb(0, 0, 0)` with no alpha is almost certainly unintended — real card shadows are `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1–0.2)`. That's a design call, not a refactor call, so it shouldn't ride along silently. The point of hoisting these isn't tidiness. It's that the next agent to touch this file now copies `bg-surface-accent` forward instead of `#ff00aa`, which is precisely the propagation this detector exists to stop. ## 2. `responsive_fragility` → drop the inert width, collapse the columns `fingerprint=responsive_fragility::src/Card.tsx::` · `width: 800`, `width: 720`, `fontSize: 18`, no `@media` The outer element carries both `width: 800` and `maxWidth: 1024`. The max-width is dead code — the element is always exactly 800px and can never reach 1024, so the constraint never fires. But a fixed 600px height on a component whose only prop is arbitrary `children` clips or overflows the moment content grows, and it's the same class of defect.
